abstract: Study the effect of AS03 adjuvant on the innate/early immune response to H5N1, avian flu, a potentially lethal disease that most subjects are assumed to be naive to. AS03 is an adjuvant oil in water emulsion containing DL-alpha-tocopherol, squalene and the non-ionic detergent Tween 80 that has been widely used as an adjuvant to flu vaccines produced by GlaxoSmithKline(GSK). We therefore propose to randomize up to 60 healthy volunteers into two intervention arms (25 volunteers in each arm with up to 10 total replacements in the event a volunteer does not return for the first vaccine). The first arm will receive a vaccine containing H5N1 with AS03 adjuvant, the second arm will receive H5N1 without AS03 adjuvant. Both arms will receive primary and booster vaccination followed by repeated blood sampling to evaluate the immune responses. We will apply high throughput analytic techniques and use systems biology methods to integrate the collected data and draw a description of the immune system response with and without the adjuvant. The primary objective is to compare multiplex immune response signatures following two (primary and a boost) vaccinations with the GSK AS03 adjuvanted H5N1 influenza vaccine or the non-adjuvanted form of the H5N1 influenza vaccine, at the 3.75 mcg dose and given 21 days apart and identify differences in very early innate immune responses. These immune signatures will also be correlated with the clinical observations especially safety related local and systemic events.

keywords: Primary Endpoint(s) 1. Identification of fine-grained innate and possible adaptive immune signatures (traditional immune parameters measurements + array-based gene expression) at all time points after primary vaccination at Day 0, within the first 24 hrs after boosting at day 21, and at D28, D42, and D100. 2. Measurement of adaptive immune responses [microneutralization (MN) titers] at Day 0, D7, D21, 28, and D100 post first vaccination (D0) and post second vaccination (D21) with or without adjuvant. 3. Correlation of pre-vaccination (D0) and post-vaccination (2-24 hrs, D7, D21 [0-24h], D28, D42, and D100 immune signatures to adaptive immune responses [microneutralization (MN) titers] on D0, D7, D21, D28, and D100 after vaccination with or without adjuvant. 3. Correlation of pre-vaccination (D0) and post-vaccination (2-24 hrs, D7, D21 [0-24h], D28, D42, and D100 immune signatures to clinical observations especially safety related local and systemic events recorded on the targeted CRF. 4. Comparison of kinetics and magnitude of vaccine-specific plasmablasts (D7, D21 and D28, D42) and memory B cells (D0, D21, D42 and D100) in participants receiving the vaccines with or without adjuvant. 5. Identification of correlative and predictive signatures of immune responses using data obtained at D0 before vaccination, and at 2-24 hrs as well as D7 and D21 days (0-24 hrs) after vaccination that correlate with MN titers at D100 in participants receiving the vaccines with or without adjuvant. Exploratory Endpoint(s) 1. T cell follicular response dynamics using flow cytometric analysis at D7, D21, D28, and D42 in participants receiving the vaccines with or without adjuvant. 2. Identification of signatures of immune responses at D0, first 24 hrs, D7, and D21 (2-24 hrs) after each vaccination that correlate with antigen-specific T cell responses at D1, D7, D21, D22, D28, and D42; and T cell follicular responses at D1, D7, D21, D22, D28, and D42 in participants receiving the vaccines with or without adjuvant. 3. Correlation of MN titers 21 days after each vaccination with antigen-specific T cell responses at D1, D7, D21, D22, D28, and D42 and T cell follicular responses at D1, D7, D21, D22, D28, and D42 in participants receiving the vaccines with or without adjuvant.
